Connection ​

Skapi ​

swift
import Skapi

let skapi = try Skapi(projectId: String, storage: SkapiStorage? = nil, timeout: TimeInterval = 120, targetCDN: String? = nil,
                      encryption: EncryptionOptions? = nil, urlSession: URLSession = .shared, observeAppLifecycle: Bool = true)
argument
projectIdthe Project ID from your project's Settings page on skapi.com
storagewhere the signed-in session is kept between launches. Left out: the Keychain on iOS and macOS (one Keychain service per project), memory elsewhere. MemoryStorage() forgets the session when the object goes away. See Storage and Keeping users signed in.
timeoutseconds to wait for each request
targetCDNleave it out. The CDN the project's endpoint list is read from.
encryptionEncryptionOptions() or your own options: encrypts the data of private records on this device before upload. See EncryptionOptions.
urlSessionthe URLSession requests go through
observeAppLifecycletrue: when the app comes back to the foreground or the network returns, a dropped realtime connection reconnects at once and an anonymous account is checked. false: call appDidReturn() yourself. See App lifecycle.

The initializer only checks the Project ID: the object connects on its first call.

Properties:

property
projectId, service, ownerthe project, read without await
version"2.4.0", read without await
await skapi.userthe signed-in profile (JSON?), see user
await skapi.sessionthe tokens (SkapiSession?): .idToken.jwtToken, .accessToken.jwtToken, .refreshToken
await skapi.connectionthe last connection info from the server (JSONObject?)

Errors ​

codemessage
INVALID_PARAMETERProject ID is required. / Project ID is invalid.
INVALID_PARAMETER"encryption.iterations" must be at least 100000.
NOT_EXISTSThe project ID does not exist. Create your project from skapi.com (thrown by the first call)

getConnectionInfo ​

swift
func getConnectionInfo(refresh: Bool = false) async throws -> JSON

The project's name and settings, and the caller as the server sees it. refresh: true asks the server again instead of using the answer from the first call.

json
{
    "project_id": "...",
    "user_ip": "203.0.113.7",
    "user_agent": "MyApp/1 CFNetwork/1490.0.4 Darwin/23.2.0",
    "user_location": "KR",
    "service_name": "My Project",
    "version": "2.4.0",
    "ai_agent": null,
    "conf": {"prevent_signup": false, "require_login": false, "anonymous_login": false, ...},
    "encryption_recovery": {"code": null, "message": "..."}
}

"encryption_recovery" is there only with encryption on and a signed-in user. It holds the user's encryption recovery code on the first call after it was created (their first password login with encryption on), and null after that, with a "message" saying what to do. See Encryption recovery codes.

appDidReturn ​

swift
func appDidReturn() async

Call it when your app comes back to the foreground, if you made the object with observeAppLifecycle: false; otherwise it runs on its own. A realtime connection that died meanwhile reconnects at once, one that looks open is asked whether it is alive, and an anonymous account is checked so a deleted one is signed out right away. See App lifecycle.

swift
// SwiftUI
.onChange(of: scenePhase) { phase in
    if phase == .active { Task { await skapi.appDidReturn() } }
}

Storage ​

swift
protocol SkapiStorage: AnyObject, Sendable {
    func getItem(_ key: String) -> String?
    func setItem(_ key: String, _ value: String)
    func removeItem(_ key: String)
}

Where the signed-in session is kept. skapi-swift stores the same keys skapi-js keeps in localStorage (the user's ID, access and refresh tokens). Logging out removes them.

type
KeychainStorage(service: String, accessGroup: String? = nil, thisDeviceOnly: Bool = false)The Keychain, one generic password item per key under service. The default on iOS and macOS, with the service "skapi.session.<service id>". accessGroup shares the session with your app extensions; thisDeviceOnly: true keeps the items out of backups and off other devices. Items stay readable after the first unlock, so a token refresh can run in the background.
MemoryStorage()Kept for the life of the Skapi object only. The default on other platforms.
FileStorage(path: String) / FileStorage(url: URL)One JSON file, created readable by the current user only (mode 600). For command line tools on macOS and Linux.
your own typeAny class conforming to SkapiStorage, for example to keep sessions in your own encrypted database.
swift
let skapi = try Skapi(projectId: "<Project ID>",
                      storage: KeychainStorage(service: "skapi.session", accessGroup: "ABCDE12345.com.example.shared"))

FetchOptions ​

swift
struct FetchOptions {
    init(limit: Int? = nil, fetchMore: Bool = false, ascending: Bool? = nil, startKey: JSON? = nil)
}

Paging for every method that takes fetchOptions:. See Paging.

field
limitRecords per call, up to 1000. The server's default is 50.
fetchMorefalse (default) starts from the first page. true reads the page after the last one this object fetched for the same query.
ascendingtrue oldest (or smallest) first, false the reverse. Left out: the method's default.
startKeyStart from this key, taken from an earlier answer, or "start" / "end".

Methods that take it return {"list": [...], "startKey": ..., "endOfList": Bool, "startKeyHistory": [...]}.

codemessage
INVALID_REQUESTFetch limit should be below 1000.
INVALID_PARAMETER"<value>" is invalid startKey key.

JSON ​

swift
enum JSON {
    case null
    case bool(Bool)
    case number(Double)
    case string(String)
    case array([JSON])
    case object(JSONObject)
}

Record data, queries, configs and answers are all JSON values, with the same keys skapi-js uses. See JSON values.

Writing:

  • Literals work: ["table": ["name": "posts", "access_group": "public"], "limit": 10, "tags": ["a", "b"]]. nil inside a literal is .null.
  • From variables: .string(title), .number(Double(count)), .bool(flag), or JSON(title), JSON(count), JSON(flag), JSON(optionalString) (nil becomes .null).
  • json["key"] = value sets a member of an object; setting nil removes it.

Reading:

member
json["key"]a member of an object, JSON?
json[0]an element of an array, JSON?
.string, .bool, .number, .array, .objectthe value, or nil for another type
.inta number that is a whole number, as Int
.isNulltrue for .null
.jsonStringcompact JSON text
JSON.parse(_ text: String) / JSON.parse(_ data: Data)parses JSON text; object keys keep their order
swift
let title = record["data"]?["title"]?.string ?? ""
let views = record["data"]?["views"]?.int ?? 0

Codable:

swift
struct Post: Codable { var title: String; var body: String }

let data = try JSON(encoding: Post(title: "Hello", body: "Hi"))
let post = try record["data"]!.decode(Post.self)

JSONObject is an object whose keys keep the order they were written in, so a value serializes the way skapi-js would write it. It has keys, values, count, isEmpty, contains(_:), removeValue(forKey:), a key subscript and dictionary (a plain [String: JSON], order lost). Numbers are Double, as in JavaScript.

SkapiError ​

swift
struct SkapiError: Error {
    let code: String
    let message: String
    let cause: Any?
}

Every error the SDK throws. code is a short name such as INVALID_PARAMETER, message says what went wrong in plain words, and cause is the underlying error when there is one. For a refused ticket, cause is the whole error body as JSON:

swift
do {
    _ = try await skapi.consumeTicket(ticketId: "launch-coupon", method: "GET", data: ["code": "WRONG"])
} catch let err as SkapiError {
    print(err.code, err.message)
    print((err.cause as? JSON)?["stage"]?.string ?? "")
}

String(describing: err) and err.localizedDescription read "<code>: <message>". The codes are listed in Errors.
